newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid frigid temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid frigid temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast Tuesday held mostly steady from Monday's levels on forecast of sustained, frigid temperatures before the end of the week.
"I don't see much of a difference. It seems the (weather) pattern is holding," said a New York electricity trader.

Weather Services Corp projected chances of precipitation Wednesday and Thursday with readings Wednesday and Thursday running three to six Fahrenheit degrees below normal, then plummeting 15-30 degrees below normal Friday and this weekend.
Day-ahead power prices in the region held most of Monday's gains despite a slight ease from the cold spell over the 48 hours, according to market sources.
Hourly dispatch rate in the Northeast during today's peak demand periods was discussed as high as $40.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Monday's high in a $45.00-$50.00 range.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Wednesday delivery in the eastern part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) were valued near $32.00-$35.00, flat from Monday's $32.00-$35.00 for Tuesday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP remained in a $22.00-$24.00 range.

In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Wednesday stayed at $28.00-$29.00 despite lower prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool, where day-ahead power fell four to five dollars from Monday.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Wednesday was again discussed at $15.00-$16.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for day-ahead delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border were a tad lower at $34.00-$36.00 from Monday's $35.00-$36.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border softened to $22.00-$26.00 from $23.00-$26.00 Monday.
Day-ahead electricity for peak, non-firm delivery at the Quebec-Northeast border stayed at $24.00-$25.00/MWh, flat from Monday.

Swing natural gas prices slipped on outlook of a brief break in the extreme chill. Next-day gas deliveries at the New York City gate dropped to $4.25 per million British thermal unit level, down from Monday's $5.00 mark.
